General Description

BeOne Medicines is seeking an experienced Project Manager to lead and coordinate a global transition of Tax and Accounting services from an incumbent external service provider to a new service provider.

Working closely with Accounting and Tax leadership, this role will coordinate internal stakeholders, the incumbent provider, the incoming provider, and regional teams to plan and execute the transition entity by entity. The Project Manager will establish the integrated transition plan, manage dependencies and readiness, coordinate knowledge transfer, track risks and decisions, and ensure that each entity moves through transition in a controlled and transparent manner.

The role will work primarily across Accounting and Tax, with coordination across Treasury and other Finance functions where services, processes, systems, or dependencies overlap. Success will require strong project management discipline, experience managing complex vendor transitions, and the ability to bring structure, accountability, and momentum to a global, cross-functional initiative.

This is a hands-on position for someone who can independently lead a complex provider-to-provider transition, organize multiple parties around a common plan, identify issues early, and diplomatically hold internal and external stakeholders accountable for commitments.

Essential Functions Of The Job

Lead planning and execution of a global transition of Tax and Accounting services from the current provider to a new service provider.
Develop and maintain integrated project plans, timelines, milestones, dependencies, and transition roadmaps.
Coordinate activities across Accounting, Tax, Treasury, regional teams, and external service providers.
Manage entity-by-entity transition activities from initial planning through cutover and stabilization.
Establish and maintain governance processes, including status meetings, steering committee updates, RAID logs, action-item tracking, and decision logs.
Identify risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and timeline conflicts early and drive mitigation plans to resolution.
Facilitate working sessions between internal teams and external partners to align scope, responsibilities, deliverables, and timelines.
Coordinate knowledge-transfer activities between the incumbent provider, BeOne teams, and the incoming provider.
Track transition readiness and ensure required documentation, training, controls, and support processes are in place before go-live.
Manage transition issues, escalations, and decision points, ensuring appropriate resolution and leadership visibility.
Prepare executive-level communications, project status updates, dashboards, and leadership presentations.
Coordinate testing, validation, business sign-off, and cutover activities required for successful service transitions.
Monitor post-transition stabilization activities and ensure issues are resolved and ownership is transferred to operational teams.
Track external providers against project commitments, deliverables, timelines, and expected outcomes.
Partner with leadership to ensure transition objectives, priorities, and resource needs remain aligned throughout the engagement.
Build trusted relationships and work effectively across global teams, time zones, cultures, and functional areas.

Education/Experience Required

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in project management, preferably in finance or accounting transitions.
Proven experience managing complex vendor transitions.
Strong project management discipline and ability to lead cross-functional initiatives.

Preferred/Nice To Have

PMP certification or equivalent project management credentials.
Experience working in a global environment with cross-functional teams.
Knowledge of Tax and Accounting processes and systems.

Join the Mission to Strengthen Arizona’s Foster Care Community!

The Arizona Department of Child Safety’s Office of Licensing and Regulation (OLR) is looking for a dynamic, mission-driven professional to help elevate foster care recruitment and retention across the state. In this role, you will report to the Caregiver Supports Supervisor and play a key part in expanding the network of incredible caregivers who support Arizona’s children.

As the leader of statewide foster recruitment and retention initiatives, you’ll collaborate closely with foster care agencies, community partners, and internal DCS teams to bring strategic, innovative solutions to life. Your work will directly shape how Arizona attracts, supports, and retains foster families—ensuring children receive safe, stable, and loving homes.

You will also analyze key data trends, identify gaps, and turn insights into actionable strategies that make a real impact. If you're energized by meaningful work, community collaboration, and improving outcomes for children and families, this is your opportunity to make a difference on a statewide level.

Coordinates planning strategies with other departments working particularly close with the DCS Communications Department, as well as other agencies. This position is responsible for collaborating with the Communication and Marketing teams to support foster home recruitment, including marketing strategies necessary for informing the public of the continuous need for foster homes.

Care Manager RN at Providence St. Mary Medical Center in Apple Valley, CA. This position is Full time and will work 12-hour, Night shifts.

Case Management is a collaborative practice including patients, caregivers, nurses, social workers, physicians, payers, support staff, other practitioners and the community. The Case Management process facilitates communication and care coordination along a continuum through effective transitional care management. Recognizing the patient's right to self-determination, the significance of the social determinants of health and the complexities of care.

Providence St. Mary Medical Center has been a part of the community of Apply Valley, California since 1956 and is recognized as one of the best regional hospitals in 6 types of care by U.S. News & World Report. Be part of our team dedicated to providing exceptional medical care across a range of specialties for our community.

Providence caregivers are not simply valued – they’re invaluable. Join our team at St. Mary Medical Center and thrive in our culture of patient-focused, whole-person care built on understanding, commitment, and mutual respect. Your voice matters here, because we know that to inspire and retain the best people, we must empower them.

Our best-in-class benefits are uniquely designed to support you and your family in staying well, growing professionally, and achieving financial security. We take care of you, so you can focus on delivering our Mission of caring for everyone, especially the most vulnerable in our communities.

new_jobs.description:
Description:

Seaford House Therapeutic Residence is seeking a Program Manager 

Lead a therapeutic residence where skilled teams help children and adolescents build safety, stability, and hope.
Seaford House is seeking an experienced, mission-driven Program Manager to lead a therapeutic residential program serving young people with behavioral and emotional needs. This is an opportunity to shape a strong trauma-informed culture, develop talented staff, and bring clinical, residential, educational, medical, and case management services together around each youth. 

Reporting to the Chief Program Officer, you will be the program’s primary operational leader—responsible for safety, service quality, staff performance, regulatory readiness, and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate combines sound clinical judgment with hands-on operational leadership and knows how to create a structured, supportive environment in which youth and staff can thrive.

As Program Manager, you will influence the full experience of Seaford House—from the quality of day-to-day care to the strength of the team delivering it. 

You will:
Build and sustain a safe, structured, trauma-informed therapeutic environment.
Coach and develop program leaders and frontline teams.
Align clinical and residential practices around individualized youth needs.
Use data, incident trends, and outcomes to improve quality and reduce risk.
Strengthen collaboration with families, funders, regulators, schools, courts, providers, and community partners.
What You’ll Lead
People and culture: Recruit, supervise, evaluate, coach, and develop Youth Advocate Supervisors, the Clinical Team Leader, and other assigned staff; promote communication, accountability, teamwork, and professional growth.
Integrated care: Coordinate clinical, residential, educational, medical, recreational, and case management services so that programming is consistent, individualized, and responsive to youth needs.
Program operations: Oversee daily operations, staffing patterns, scheduling, referrals, admissions, census, utilization, facility needs, resources, and contract performance.
Safety and crisis leadership: Support staff during crises; review serious incidents, restraints, unauthorized absences, police involvement, contraband concerns, and other significant events; ensure timely documentation, communication, reporting, and follow-up.
Quality and compliance: Maintain readiness for licensing and accreditation; oversee incident reports, corrective action plans, records, required training, certifications, audits, and regulatory or contractual reporting.
Performance improvement: Monitor program data, incident trends, youth feedback, engagement, and outcomes; identify opportunities and implement practical improvements that strengthen safety, stability, and service quality.
Community partnership: Build productive relationships with families, funders, regulators, schools, courts, providers, law enforcement, and other stakeholders.
Mission support: Participate in agency meetings, committees, court proceedings, and community activities, and step into direct service when needed.

Schedule and Position Requirements

Residential care requires visible, responsive leadership. This site-based role has a schedule that varies with program needs and may include evenings, weekends, holidays, on-call rotation, and crisis response outside traditional business hours.
Ability to interpret and apply agency policies, licensing regulations, accreditation standards, contractual requirements, and best practices.
Completion of required annual training and maintenance of applicable certifications under OCCL requirements.
Reliable transportation and a valid driver’s license that meets the requirements of the agency’s insurance carrier. 
Commitment to culturally responsive practice, confidentiality, professionalism, quality, and accountability.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

Master's degree in Social Work, Counseling, Psychology, Human Services Administration, Public Administration, or a related field required.
Clinical licensure preferred.
Five (5) or more years of experience working with adolescents, child welfare-involved youth, youth with behavioral or emotional challenges, or youth in residential treatment settings preferred.
Previous supervisory or management experience required. Experience managing residential, behavioral health, child welfare, juvenile justice, or youth-serving programs strongly preferred.

Job Description

About Us:

Affinity Hospice is one of the fastest growing, privately held hospice organizations in the country. We are passionate about giving exceptional care to our hospice patients and their families. We believe the care we provide truly matters and we would love to have you join our nationally recognized team!  

What We Offer:  

Paid Time Off (PTO), Sick Time, and Holiday Pay 
Gas Card and Car Maintenance Stipend  
Benefit Package (Medical, Dental, Vision and more) for full-time employees  
401K 
Employee Assistance Program  
Tuition Reimbursement for eligible employees 
Internal Company Advancement
Free end of life training  

Position Summary: 

The registered nurse/case manager plans, organizes, directs, and provides hospice care and is experienced in nursing, with emphasis on community health education and experience.  The professional nurse builds from the resources of the community to plan and direct services to meet the needs of individual and families within their homes and communities.  

Hours / Schedule:
 Full Time; (40) hours / week.

Minimum Qualifications:  

Graduate of an accredited Diploma, Associate or Baccalaureate School of Nursing.
Current State license as a Registered Nurse
Current CPR certification
Minimum of two years of experience as a Registered Nurse in a clinical care, home health or hospice setting preferred.
Must be a licensed driver with an automobile that is insured in accordance with state and/or organization requirements and is in good working order.  
Excellent observation, verbal and written communication skills, problem solving skills, basic math skills; nursing skills per competency checklist.  
Able to lift, position and/or transfer patients.    
Able to lift supplies and equipment.   

Key Responsibilities:

Case manages and provides clinical direction to the interdisciplinary team, physician, and family.
Implement/develop/document the patient plan of care
Provide care utilizing infection control measures that protect both the staff and the patient (OSHA).
Assure continuity of quality patient care delivered with appropriate documentation.
Monitor assigned cases to ensure compliance with requirements of third-party payer.
Demonstrate commitment, professional growth, and competency.
Promote agency philosophy and administrative policies.
Perform on-call responsibilities and provide on-call service to patients/families as assigned.
Responsible for supervising hospice aides and licensed practical nurses. 
Perform other nursing duties as assigned by management to support department goals and initiatives.
